episodes.191408: During the morning and early afternoon hours of July 1st, heavy rainfall yielded flash flooding across much of Johnson County. A swath of 3 to 6 of rain with isolated locations up to 7 fell within about a 3 hour time period from about 930 am to 1230 pm.
episodes.191409: During the morning and early afternoon hours of July 1st, heavy rainfall yielded flash flooding across much of the southern two thirds of Jackson County. A swath of 3 to 6 of rain with isolated locations up to 7 fell within about a 3 hour time period from about 930 am to 1230 pm.
episodes.191433: A line of strong/severe storms tracked across eastern Elbert and Lincoln Counties during the early evening of June 30th producing hail up to one inch in diameter and 60 mph wind gusts.
episodes.191445: Several bands and clusters of thunderstorms produced scattered instances of wind damage mainly near and east of Interstate 95 in Maryland and northern Virginia. There were a few instances of considerable wind damage in Maryland.
episodes.191449: Multiple bands and clusters of thunderstorms produced strong winds over area waterways during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.191533: A wave of scattered to numerous showers and storms developed from the northern Coastal Plain into the eastern Sandhills and southern Coastal Plain late in the evening of June 30th and continued into the morning hours of July 1st. This wave of storms was along a cold front sliding south from the Ohio Valley. Several inches of rain led to flash flooding in Sampson County.
episodes.191541: A severe thunderstorm resulted in a recorded wind gust of 66 mph at San Simon.
episodes.191603: An upper level disturbance moving across the Great Basin and Central Rockies combined with record levels of monsoon moisture resulted in the development of widespread showers and storms across northern and central NM each and every afternoon from July 1st through July 3rd. These thunderstorms produced high wind gusts of 59 and 68 mph at the Belen Regional Airport and the Mine mesonet station on the White Sands Missile Range respectively on July 1st. There was a 59 mph wind gust at the Raton Crews Airport on July 3rd. Drier air moved in from the northwest on the backside of the disturbance on July 4th.
episodes.191634: Long hodographs and deep inverted-V soundings resulted in organized convection across Southwest Montana June 30. Hail was the main severe observation, but a wind gust of 58 mph was also observed.
episodes.191656: In the overnight hours of the 30th, a supercell developed in east central Colorado and moved east-northeast. As it passed near the Burlington ASOS, a 60 MPH gust was recorded.
episodes.191689: River flooding from late June continued into early July.
episodes.191782: A few strong to severe thunderstorms formed during the evening.
episodes.191933: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms impacted portions of southeast Wyoming from the mid afternoon through the early evening hours on 6/30, producing several instances of large hail in excess of one inch in diameter as well as wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH. Most notably, a cluster of intense thunderstorms tracked across central Laramie County roughly between 7 PM and 9 PM MDT, producing 70 to 80 MPH wind gusts and reportedly damaging several outbuildings in the northern outskirts of Cheyenne.
episodes.192240: During the afternoon hours a line of scattered storms developed over Northwest Kansas producing estimated gusts up to 90 mph, primarily in Thomas County, with damage to a shed, vehicle windows, and trees in the city of Colby. Additional wind gusts of 58 mph were reported near Winona in Logan County.
episodes.192848: An upper level trough was moving over Nebraska from the west. A warm front was present near the Kansas/Nebraska border. Warm, moist air was on the east side of the warm front with hot, drier conditions on the west side of the front. CAPE, wind shear, and instability were high along and to the south of the front. A surface trough was also across the area which enhanced atmospheric lift. ||Storms developed across northwest Kansas into southern Nebraska during the early to mid afternoon hours. These storms moved eastward into south central Nebraska during the early evening hours and one storm began impacting the local area by producing a 58 mph wind gust in Furnas County. This same storm ended up producing a tornado about 15 minutes later in Furnas County. This storm moved northeastward and produced another tornado in Kearney County over an hour later. Both tornadoes were rated an EFU due to lack of quality damage indicators in the area. The storms in the area produced severe wind gusts and ended with the strongest wind gust of the day of 78 mph in Fillmore County after 10 PM CDT.
episodes.192984: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon, typical of summertime. A few trees were blown down with the strongest storms. In addition, slow moving storms produced localized flash flooding.
episodes.193044: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a typical summertime environment. One storm moved over the Panama City Airport with measured wind gusts in excess of 50 knots.
episodes.193142: An isolated thunderstorm produced some large hail and severe wind gusts.
episodes.193163: A line of showers and thunderstorms passed through south-central Wyoming early morning on the 1st with gusty winds around 60 mph along Interstate 80 near Elk Mountain.
episodes.193166: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved across the central and northern Nebraska panhandle during the afternoon of the 1st. Strong winds exceeding 70 mph were observed near Chadron with a separate storm producing wind gusts around 50 mph near Scottsbluff.
episodes.193325: Widespread rainfall of two to five inches, with localized amounts of up to ten inches, produced multiple instances of flash flooding across east-central Kansas.
episodes.193378: Monsoon moisture brougth strong to severe thunderstorms to parts of northern Arizona.
episodes.193407: A thunderstorm became severe over southwest portions of Weston County and tracked northeast across the county before weakening as it moved into South Dakota. The storm produced wind gusts to 70 mph from the Rochelle area to near Newcastle.
episodes.193408: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over portions of southwest Meade County, producing large hail in the Tilford and Piedmont areas.
episodes.193409: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the Black Hawk area, producing hail to quarter size.
episodes.193410: A supercell thunderstorm developed across southern Fall River County and tracked east into Oglala Lakota County. The storm produced wind gusts to over 60 mph.
episodes.193413: A severe thunderstorm developed over Jackson County, producing wind gusts to over 75 mph over northern portions of the county.
episodes.193414: A thunderstorm became severe as it moved into central South Dakota, producing wind gusts to over 60 mph in the Midland area.
episodes.193415: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northern portions of Weston County, producing hail up to quarter size north of Osage.
episodes.193416: A supercell thunderstorm developed over Oglala Lakota County and tracked east into Bennett County, producing very large hail up to baseball size and gusty winds.
episodes.193424: A thunderstorm passing over region brought gusty winds up to 41 MPH. A power outage affecting 700 customers was attributed to the storm winds.
episodes.193809: A very warm and moist airmass was in place as a strong cold front moved into the Mid-Atlantic. This resulted in several showers and thunderstorms developing, which brought damaging wind gusts, knocking down trees and power lines across portions of New Jersey.
episodes.193873: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central, south central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.193876: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.193878: Unusually high moisture and instability values across eastern Utah and western Colorado led to widespread shower and thunderstorm activity on the 30th. These storms produced heavy rain and strong, gusty winds along with frequent lightning and some hail. The San Juan mountains and points south saw the most active weather of the event.
episodes.193888: Heavy rainfall throughout June led to many locations along the Mississippi River in northeast Iowa to enter flood stage which persisted into July. During the first week of July many points along the Mississippi River observed their maximum river stage in minor to moderate flooding. As relatively drier conditions took hold through the first half of July, river stages fell below flood stage into the middle of the month.
episodes.193889: Heavy rainfall throughout June led to many locations along the Mississippi River in Southeast Minnesota to enter flood stage which persisted into July. During the first week of July many points along the Mississippi River south of Wabasha observed their maximum river stage in minor to moderate flooding. As relatively drier conditions took hold over the first half of July, river stages fell below flood stage into the middle of the month.
episodes.193890: Heavy rainfall throughout June led to many locations along the Mississippi River in Western Wisconsin to enter flood stage which persisted into July. During the first week of July many points along the Mississippi River observed their maximum river stage in minor to moderate flooding. As relatively drier conditions took hold over the first half of July, river stages fell below flood stage into the middle of the month.
episodes.194087: Significant, and at times record, river flooding in northwest Iowa continued from June into July. Flooding resulted in massive sandbagging efforts, prolonged road closures and damages, and impacts to home and businesses. Continued heavy rain in early July kept some locations in flood through the middle of the month.
episodes.194144: A severe thunderstorm produced wind gusts to around 60 mph in the Gillette area.
episodes.194170: A cluster of thunderstorms along the Kansas-Nebraska border moved northeast into Red Willow County producing wind gusts estimated to be up to 60 mph. The strongest gust occurred southeast of McCook, Nebraska.
episodes.194174: In the late evening of June 30th, storms formed in eastern Colorado and proceeded to enter northwest Kansas near midnight. As these storms moved over Colby in the small hours of the morning, gusts around 60 MPH were recorded.
episodes.194186: River levels from the historic June flooding remained above flood stage for some locations into July, although continued a declining trend.
episodes.194192: River levels from the historic June flooding remained above flood stage for some locations into July, although continued a declining trend.
episodes.194194: River levels from the historic June flooding remained above flood stage for some locations into July, although continued a declining trend.
episodes.194289: Showers and thunderstorms developed as a cold front pushed through North Dakota. Initially, a funnel cloud formed to the east of Minot, in Ward County, along a surface boundary with rain showers and weak thunderstorms. Additional thunderstorms developed with a couple of storms becoming severe over McLean and Oliver counties. The largest hail reported was a half-dollar in size, and occurred at Center in Oliver County.
episodes.194460: A surface trough existed near the Continental Divide while a broad upper trough was moving through the Great Basin.  Deeper moisture existed west of the Divide and helped fuel storms over the Gila region where a wind gust to 60 mph was recorded in Silver City.
episodes.194624: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a cold front produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.194625: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.194814: A deep subtropical moisture plume remained in place as a deep low pressure trough and cold front moved across the area, resulting in strong thunderstorms that produced heavy rain rates and flash flooding in some areas. One particular storm resulted in a debris flow across Pitkin County.
episodes.195128: Many thunderstorms produced severe wind gust speeds.
episodes.195173: At the beginning of July, river flooding was still ongoing along portions of the Missouri River extending from east-central Nebraska/southwest Iowa to the southern Nebraska border. Most of the length of the river crested at the end of June, so the greatest impacts are addressed in June StormData. However, sections of I-29 and the I-29/I680 junction remained closed through the first week of July as flood waters receded. There were also riverfront properties in far southeast Nebraska that were flooded this first week of July as well.||On the morning of July 1st, a trough positioned over the Rockies ejected out into the central Plains. At the surface, a low pressure developed in the central High Plains in response to this upper level feature, with a quasi-stationary warm front draped from central Nebraska southeast into the lower Mississippi River Valley. Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed along and north of this frontal zone by the evening hours, resulting in widespread heavy rain across much of southeast Nebraska into southwest Iowa. Sporadic severe weather also occurred, primarily focused in Lincoln and surrounding areas. This included an EF-0 in Saline County and an EF-1 just southwest of Lincoln. Training thunderstorms produced flash flooding across much of the I-80 corridor between Lincoln and Omaha. A Flash Flood Emergency was issued for locations around Horseshoe Lake in Cass County due to water rapidly rising and trapping multiple people in their homes.

This is a continuation of river flooding from the end of June. River levels crested along this stretch of the Missouri at the end of June, hence flood waters were receding by this time. As such, the greatest impacts were felt in June (and discussed in the June entry for StormData). For the first part of July while flood waters continued to recede, continued impacts were felt in the form of residual flooding in low-lying areas of roads, trails, and riverfront properties. Any property damages associated with this event are in June StormData to coincide with when the river crested. As such, have set damages for this entry to zero.
